data.title: Bài 29: The Bicycle Repair Shop
data.transcript: Near the university, there is a small bicycle repair shop owned by Mr. Ba. The shop has no sign, only a pile of old tires and a blue toolbox. Mr. Ba is seventy years old but his hands are strong and skilled. One day, Tuan's bicycle chain broke on the way to work. He pushed his bicycle to Mr. Ba's shop. Mr. Ba did not say much. He looked at the chain, cleaned it with an old cloth, and added some oil. Within five minutes, the bicycle was fixed. Tuan asked how much, and Mr. Ba said, Just two thousand dong for the oil. Tuan was surprised. He offered more, but Mr. Ba refused. He said, I like to help students. If your bicycle works, you can go to school. That afternoon, Tuan returned with two cold lemon teas. They sat together and talked about how the city has changed. Mr. Ba said he has repaired bicycles for fifty years and has seen thousands of students grow up. Tuan learned that true success is not about money. It is about being useful to your community for a long time.

data.title: Bài 30: A Day Without Smartphone
data.transcript: Last Sunday, Tuan decided to have a day without his smartphone. He turned it off and put it in a drawer. At first, he felt nervous. His hand kept reaching for his pocket. He did not know what time it was or what the news was. He went for a walk in the park without music or maps. He noticed things he had never seen before: the shape of the leaves, the way the old people played chess, and how children laughed without taking photos. He sat on a bench and read a paper book for two hours. His mind felt calm and clear. In the afternoon, he visited his parents and talked with them without checking his phone once. His mother said, You look more relaxed today. That night, he wrote in his journal. He realized the phone is a powerful tool, but it should not control his life. From now on, he decided to have one hour every evening with no screen, just thinking, reading, or talking with family. That small habit changed his focus completely.

data.title: Bài 31: The English Notebook
data.transcript: When Tuan was fifteen, he had a small green notebook. On the cover, he wrote My English Dream. Every day, he wrote five new English words and one sentence. Some days he was busy with school, but he never missed a day. The notebook became thick and dirty, but he loved it. One word was sunrise. He wrote, I woke up early to see the sunrise over the rice fields. Another word was promise. He wrote, I promise to study English every day. His friends laughed and said a notebook cannot change your life. But after three years, Tuan could speak English fluently while his friends were still struggling. When he built TuanQK Education, he remembered that green notebook. He told his team, Big dreams are built from small, consistent actions. You do not need expensive courses. You need a small notebook, a pen, and the discipline to write every day. That notebook is still on his desk today as a reminder that consistency beats talent.

data.title: Bài 32: The Rainy Library
data.transcript: It was raining heavily, and Lisa was stuck in the old city library. The lights flickered, but the library was warm and quiet. She walked between the tall bookshelves and found a book about Vietnam in English. She sat down and started reading. The book told stories about festivals, myths, and the meaning of Tet. She had never read about her own culture in English before. It felt strange and exciting. She started to translate the stories in her head. How would she explain banh chung to a foreign friend? How would she describe the dragon dance? She took out her phone and recorded herself speaking in English for three minutes. Her voice was shaky, but she continued. After the rain stopped, she walked home with a new idea. She would create short English videos about Vietnamese culture for her app. She realized the best way to learn English is not just to study American or British culture, but to use English to tell your own story. That rainy afternoon in the library changed her direction.

data.title: Bài 33: The Night Bus to Ha Giang
data.transcript: Tuan took a night bus to Ha Giang, a mountainous area in the north. The bus was crowded and the road was bumpy. He could not sleep. He looked out the window and saw stars brighter than ever before. At four in the morning, the bus arrived. The air was freezing cold. He rented a motorbike and drove slowly through the fog. The mountains were huge and silent. He met children on the way to school wearing colorful clothes. They waved and shouted Hello in English. He stopped at a small homestay where a family offered him hot tea and corn cake. They did not speak English, but they communicated with smiles and gestures. That night, Tuan sat outside and looked at the sky. He thought about how language connects people, but kindness connects them even without language. He decided to add a lesson in his app about travel English, but also about respectful gestures when you travel. Language is important, but a sincere smile is universal.

data.title: Bài 34: Fixing a Bug at Midnight
data.transcript: It was midnight, and the office was dark except for Tuan's computer light. He was fixing a serious bug in the Music Study feature. The app crashed every time a user played a song with no lyrics file. He had tried three different solutions, but none worked. He felt tired and frustrated. He made some instant coffee and opened the error log again. He read each line slowly. Suddenly, he saw it. The code tried to read a file that did not exist, and there was no check for null. He added a simple if statement to check if the file exists before reading. He built the app again and tested it. It worked perfectly. The music played, and the screen showed No lyrics yet instead of crashing. He smiled and leaned back in his chair. He learned that most big bugs come from small missing checks. He wrote a note for his team: Always assume files can be missing. Always write safe code. That note is now a rule in TuanQK Education development.

data.title: Bài 35: The Letter to My Future Self
data.transcript: In the final lesson of the year, Lisa asked her students to write a letter to their future selves in English. Tuan wrote his letter carefully. He wrote, Dear future Tuan, I hope you are still curious. I hope you still wake up early to learn new things. Today, our app has 500 lessons. I hope in the future it has 5000 lessons and helps millions of people. Please remember why we started. We did not start to make money. We started to help Vietnamese students speak English with confidence. Don't forget to call your parents every day. Don't forget to drink water and exercise. And don't forget to be kind to your team. Love, Tuan from 2025. He sealed the letter and put it in his drawer. He planned to open it in five years. His students were quiet after reading their letters. One student cried because she had never thought about her future so clearly. Lisa said, Writing to your future self is not just an English exercise. It is a way to make a promise to yourself.

data.title: Bài 36: The Power of Listening
data.transcript: Many students think speaking is the most important skill in English. But Tuan believes listening is even more important. He tells a story about his first job interview in English. He was nervous and spoke very fast, trying to show his vocabulary. But he did not listen to the interviewer's question carefully. He answered the wrong question. He failed the interview. After that, he practiced listening every day for one hour. He listened to podcasts, conversations, and news without subtitles. Slowly, he started to hear not just words, but meaning and emotion. In the next interview, he listened carefully, paused, and answered clearly. He got the job. In TuanQK Education, every listening lesson starts with Step 1 Listen before Speak. He tells students, If you listen well, speaking becomes natural. Listening is not passive. It is an active act of respect. When you truly listen to someone, you make them feel valued. That is why listening is the first step in learning and in life.

data.title: Bài 37: The Small Coffee Shop
data.transcript: On Le Loi street, there is a small coffee shop with only three tables. The owner is a young woman named Mai who loves English. She puts English quotes on the wall and plays English songs softly. Tuan goes there every Friday to work. He orders black coffee with no sugar. Mai always asks him, What new word did you learn today? One Friday, Tuan taught her the word cozy. He said, Your shop is very cozy. It means warm, comfortable, and small in a good way. Mai loved the word. She wrote it on her menu board. Next week, Tuan saw that she had added a new drink called Cozy Latte. Customers liked it. Mai told Tuan that learning one English word helped her business. She started to label all her drinks in both Vietnamese and English. Tourists came more often because they could understand the menu. Tuan realized that English is not just for exams. It is a tool to make your small world bigger and more welcoming. A single word can change a small shop.

data.title: Bài 38: The Midnight Train Sound
data.transcript: Tuan lives near the railway, and every night at eleven, a midnight train passes by. The sound is loud and long. At first, he complained about the noise. He could not sleep well. But then he started to use the sound as a reminder. When he heard the train, he stopped working and took five deep breaths. He asked himself, What did I do well today? What can I do better tomorrow? The train became his daily reflection bell. One night, his younger brother visited and asked why he smiled when the train passed. Tuan explained his habit. His brother laughed and said, You turned noise into a teacher. Tuan added a small feature in his app called Night Reflection. At 11 PM, the app asks, What is one good thing that happened today? Many users love it. They say it helps them sleep with a positive mind. Tuan learned that you cannot always control the sounds around you, but you can change what they mean to you. The train still passes every night, but now it brings peace, not annoyance.

data.title: Bài 39: How to Say Sorry in English
data.transcript: Lisa noticed Vietnamese students often say sorry too much or too little in English. She created a lesson about apologizing. She explained that Sorry is not just a word, it has levels. If you step on someone's foot lightly, you say, Oh, sorry. If you are late for a meeting, you say, I am sorry I am late. I had traffic. If you make a serious mistake at work, you say, I sincerely apologize for the error. I will fix it immediately. She asked students to role-play. Tuan played a manager and Lisa played an employee who forgot a report. Lisa said, I apologize for missing the deadline. I take full responsibility and I will send it tonight. Tuan was impressed. He said a good apology has three parts: admit, explain briefly, and offer a solution. Never make a long excuse. After the class, a student said he used the lesson to apologize to his foreign boss and the boss appreciated his professionalism. Lisa smiled. Language is not just grammar. It is also knowing how to handle difficult moments with grace.

data.title: Bài 40: The Old Dictionary
data.transcript: Tuan's father gave him an old English Vietnamese dictionary. The book is thick, yellow, and smells like old paper. It was published in 1998. Tuan's father bought it when he was young and dreamed of learning English, but he never had time because he worked in the fields. Now he gave it to Tuan and said, Maybe you will use it more than me. Tuan did not use it to look up words because he has apps now. Instead, he keeps it on his desk. When he feels lazy, he looks at the dictionary and remembers his father's dream. His father could not learn English, but he wanted his son to have the chance. Tuan added a feature in the app called Word History. Every time you learn a word, you can see its history and example. He wants learning to feel personal, not just digital. Last week, he taught his father the word dictionary in English. His father laughed loudly and repeated it five times. That old book is not just paper. It is a bridge between two generations and two dreams.

data.title: Bài 41: The First Presentation
data.transcript: Lisa remembered her first presentation in English at university. Her hands were sweating and her voice was shaking. She had prepared twenty slides with too much text. She read every word from the slides and never looked at the audience. After five minutes, people started to check their phones. She finished quickly and sat down feeling embarrassed. Her teacher came to her and said gently, A presentation is not about slides. It is about connection. Next time, try to tell a story with only three main points. Lisa practiced for months. She learned to start with a question, use one clear picture per slide, and make eye contact. A year later, she presented again about learning apps. She started with, Have you ever felt nervous speaking English? Everyone nodded. She spoke slowly, smiled, and used simple words. People listened and asked questions. She got the highest score. Now she teaches her students in TuanQK Education, Don't try to impress with big words. Try to connect with simple words and a true story. That is good communication.

data.title: Bài 42: The Gardener and the Seeds
data.transcript: Behind TuanQK Tower, there is a small garden cared for by Uncle Hai. He grows tomatoes, mint, and sunflowers. Tuan once asked him, How do you grow such beautiful plants? Uncle Hai said, I don't grow plants. I take care of the soil, water, and sunlight. The plants grow by themselves. Tuan thought about this for a long time. He realized learning English is similar. Many students try to force themselves to memorize, but they forget quickly. Instead, if you create a good environment, English grows naturally. Good soil means good habits, like reading ten minutes every morning. Water means listening to English every day. Sunlight means speaking without fear of mistakes. Tuan told his team this story, and they changed their teaching method. Instead of forcing students to do many boring exercises, they created a daily environment: a short video, a small speaking task, and a kind community. Students started to enjoy learning. Uncle Hai's garden taught Tuan a powerful lesson. Don't push the flower to bloom faster. Just take care of the conditions, and it will bloom in its own time.

data.title: Bài 43: The Lost Key and Found Friendship
data.transcript: Lisa lost her house key on a crowded bus. She was very stressed because her landlord lived far away. She posted in a Facebook group in English and Vietnamese, asking if anyone found a key with a blue rabbit keychain. An hour later, a university student named Minh messaged her. He found it on the bus and kept it safe. They met at a coffee shop to return the key. Minh was shy and spoke English slowly, but he tried his best. Lisa was impressed by his kindness. They talked for an hour about learning English and life in the city. They became friends and started a small English exchange club. Every Wednesday, they met to practice conversation. Minh improved his English quickly because he had a real reason to speak. Lisa learned that losing something sometimes helps you find something more valuable. She added a lesson in the app about asking for help in English, with useful sentences like I lost my key near the bus station. Has anyone seen it? A simple sentence can start a friendship and open many doors.

data.title: Bài 44: The 5 AM Club
data.transcript: Tuan joined a 5 AM club with three friends. Every morning, they woke up at five, studied English for one hour, and shared what they learned in a group chat. At first, it was very difficult. The bed was warm and the outside was dark. But after seven days, it became a habit. Tuan noticed his mind was freshest in the morning. He could remember new words better than at night. After thirty days, his friends noticed a big change in his pronunciation. One friend said, You sound more confident now. The club did not just help with English. It helped with discipline. They never blamed each other if someone missed a day. They just encouraged each other to come back. Tuan implemented this idea in TuanQK Education as a Morning Streak feature. Users who study before 6 AM get a special sunrise badge. Many users love it and say it makes them feel proud. Waking up early is not about punishing yourself. It is about giving yourself a quiet hour before the world gets noisy. That hour can change your whole day.

data.title: Bài 45: The Story of Two Turtles
data.transcript: In Hoan Kiem Lake, there is a legend about two turtles. Lisa told this story to her foreign friend in English. She said, A long time ago, a king returned a magic sword to a golden turtle in the lake. The turtle said, Thank you for protecting our country. The friend asked, Is it true? Lisa smiled and said, It is a legend, but it teaches us about gratitude. In Vietnamese culture, turtles represent wisdom and long life. Her friend loved the story and asked more about Vietnamese myths. Lisa realized she knew many Vietnamese stories but had never told them in English. She went home and wrote five traditional stories in simple English: The Story of Banh Chung, The Legend of the Watermelon, and others. She added them to the listening section of the app. Students loved them because they were familiar but practiced in a new language. Telling your own culture's stories in English is powerful. It helps you remember vocabulary because the stories are already in your heart. You just need new words to share them with the world.

data.title: Bài 46: The Empty Classroom
data.transcript: During Tet holiday, the university was empty. Tuan went to his old classroom and sat alone. The room was quiet, and the whiteboard still had some English words from the last lesson: dream, future, courage. He remembered how nervous he was when he first studied there. He could not pronounce the word comfortable. His classmates laughed, but his teacher encouraged him to try again. Now he was building an app that teaches that same word to thousands of students. He walked to the whiteboard and wrote, Thank you, teacher. He took a photo and sent it to his old teacher. The teacher replied immediately, I am proud of you. Keep helping others learn. Tuan sat there for a long time. He understood that a classroom is not just four walls. It is a place where someone believes in you before you believe in yourself. That is why he named his company Education, not just App. He wants every student using TuanQK to feel that someone believes in them, even when they study alone at night.

data.title: Bài 47: The Broken Headphones
data.transcript: Lisa's headphones broke the day before her important online English test. She had no money to buy new ones and the test required listening. She felt panicked. She tried to fix them with tape, but only one side worked. She decided to take the test anyway with one working ear. During the test, she had to focus twice as hard because she could only hear partially. Surprisingly, she got a high score. She realized that when one ear was blocked, her brain paid more attention. After the test, she shared her experience with Tuan. She said, Sometimes limitations help us focus better. Tuan added a listening exercise called One Ear Challenge where students listen with only one headphone or with background noise. It trains the brain to focus on key words, not every single word. Lisa bought new headphones later, but she kept the broken ones on her desk as a reminder. Difficult conditions are not always bad. Sometimes they force us to develop stronger skills that we would never develop in comfortable conditions.

data.title: Bài 48: The Gift of Feedback
data.transcript: Tuan was afraid of feedback. When someone criticized his app design, he felt hurt and defensive. One day, a senior developer told him, Feedback is a gift, but only if you open it. Tuan thought about this. He started to change his attitude. When a user said, Your app is confusing, he did not get angry. He asked, Can you tell me which part is confusing? I want to fix it. He listened and took notes. He improved the app quickly because he used feedback as data, not as judgment. In the listening lessons, he added a Step 2 where AI gives feedback on pronunciation. Some students feel shy when AI says their pronunciation is not perfect. Tuan tells them, AI feedback is not to judge you. It is to show you where to improve, like a mirror. If you smile at feedback and say thank you, you will grow much faster. He now asks for feedback every week from his team and users. He learned that a closed mind learns nothing, but an open mind can learn from everyone.

data.title: Bài 49: The Language of Food
data.transcript: TuanQK Education organized a small food festival for students to practice English. Each student had to introduce a Vietnamese dish in English. One student brought banh mi and said, This is banh mi. It is crunchy outside, soft inside. It has pate, pork, herbs, and chili. It is the best sandwich in the world. Everyone laughed and clapped. Another student introduced che, a sweet dessert soup. She said, This is sweet, colorful, and makes you happy when you are sad. Foreign teachers who attended the festival said they learned more about Vietnam in one hour than in one month of reading books. Tuan realized food is a powerful language. When you describe food, you use adjectives, senses, and emotions. You say it smells good, tastes sweet, feels soft. Those are important English words. He added a whole listening series about Vietnamese food in English. Students love it because they can use it immediately when they meet foreigners. If you can talk about pho, you can make a new friend in five minutes anywhere in the world.

data.title: Bài 50: The Promise on TuanQK Tower
data.transcript: TuanQK Tower is not a real tower yet. It is Tuan's dream of a future education building. On the rooftop, he imagines a garden where students can practice English under the sky. Last year, he took Ms. Ay Ai, an English teacher, to the construction site. The site was just mud and bricks. He said, One day, this will be a tower where students from all over Vietnam come to learn languages, technology, and kindness. Ms. Ay Ai smiled and said, I believe you. She recorded a video of Tuan talking about his dream. That video is now Lesson 4 in the listening section. Tuan watches it sometimes when he feels tired. It reminds him why he works so hard. He knows building a tower takes years, just like building English fluency. You need a strong foundation, good materials, and patience. Every lesson he creates is like a brick in that tower. He promised himself that he would never stop laying bricks, even if the progress is slow. Because one day, students will stand on top of that tower and see a bigger world.

data.title: Bài 51: The Art of Small Talk
data.transcript: Lisa taught a lesson about small talk, which is very important in English culture. She said many Vietnamese students are good at grammar but don't know how to start a casual conversation. She gave three magic questions: How is your day going? What did you do this weekend? Have you tried the coffee here? She asked students to practice in an elevator for thirty seconds. Tuan tried it. He met a foreign colleague in the elevator and said, How is your day going? The colleague smiled and talked about his morning meeting. In thirty seconds, they had a friendly connection. Tuan realized small talk is not small. It is a big door to relationships. He added a listening practice where students listen to two people making small talk in a coffee shop, airport, and office. The key is to listen and ask one more question, not to talk about yourself too much. Small talk shows you care about the other person. If you master it, you will never feel awkward in English again. It is like warm-up before exercise.

data.title: Bài 52: The Second-Hand Bookstore
data.transcript: There is a second-hand bookstore on a quiet street where books cost only ten thousand dong. The owner, an old man, does not use a computer. He remembers every book by memory. Tuan loves to visit and find old English books. One day, he found a book called English for Daily Life from 1985. Inside, someone had written Vietnamese translations by hand. The handwriting was neat and careful. Tuan bought the book and felt connected to the previous owner who also struggled to learn English many years ago. He thought about how many people have walked the same path of learning. He brought the book to the office and showed his team. He said, We are not just building an app. We are continuing a long journey of many learners before us. We should respect their effort by making learning easier for the next generation. He placed the old book next to his new laptop. The old and new together remind him that tools change, but the desire to learn stays the same across decades.

data.title: Bài 53: The Interview with a Child
data.transcript: For a listening lesson, Lisa interviewed a six-year-old girl named Linh in English. She asked, What is happiness? Linh answered, Happiness is when my mom makes fried rice and we eat together. Lisa asked, What is English? Linh said, English is a magic key to watch cartoons without mom translating. Everyone in the office laughed, but Tuan was moved. He realized children have the best definitions because they are simple and honest. Adults make English complicated with grammar rules and fear of mistakes. Children just use it to get what they want, like watching cartoons. Tuan added a lesson called Explain Like a Child where students have to explain big words in simple English. For example, explain democracy to a six-year-old. This exercise forces you to truly understand, not just memorize. Lisa kept interviewing children and added their answers to the app. Users love it because children's answers are funny and wise at the same time. Sometimes the best teacher is a child who is not afraid to speak.

data.title: Bài 54: The Sound of Rain on the Roof
data.transcript: In the countryside, Tuan's grandmother's house has a tin roof. When it rains, the sound is very loud and rhythmic. As a child, Tuan could not sleep during rain because of the noise. His grandmother told him to listen to the rain as music. She said, Each drop is a drum beat. Close your eyes and listen to the concert. He tried, and slowly the noise became music. Now, when he works in the city and it rains, he records the sound of rain and plays it while coding. It helps him focus. He created a listening exercise called Nature Sounds where students listen to rain, birds, and wind and then describe them in English. Words like pitter-patter, drizzle, and whisper become easy to remember when you hear the real sound. He learned that English is not just in textbooks. It is in the sounds around you. If you learn to describe the rain, you can describe your feelings too. The rain on the roof taught him to listen with imagination, not just with ears.

data.title: Bài 55: The Final Lesson is to Begin
data.transcript: After completing fifty listening lessons, Tuan's student asked, What is the final lesson? Tuan smiled and said, The final lesson is to begin. Many students wait until they are perfect to start speaking. They say, I will speak when my pronunciation is perfect. But perfect never comes. Tuan told them about his first English video. It was terrible. His pronunciation was bad and he forgot words. But he posted it anyway. People corrected him kindly, and he improved. If he had waited to be perfect, he would never have started. In TuanQK Education, lesson fifty-five is not the end. It is a reminder that learning English is a circle, not a line. You finish one round and start again with deeper understanding. The app now has fifty-five lessons, but your real lessons are in the streets, in conversations, and in mistakes you will make tomorrow. So close this app for today, go outside, and say hello to someone in English. That hello is your real final lesson and your new beginning at the same time.

data.title: Bài 63: Hòa hợp chủ ngữ - động từ (Subject-Verb Agreement)
data.theory:
1. Quy tắc cơ bản: S số ít + Vs/es, S số nhiều + V0. He lives, They live.
2. Each, Every, Everyone, Somebody, Nobody, No one, Either, Neither + V số ít: Everyone is here. Each student has a laptop.
3. Both, Many, Few + V số nhiều: Both are good. Many people are waiting.
4. Chủ ngữ dài: Động từ chia theo chủ ngữ CHÍNH, không theo danh từ xen giữa: The book on the tables is mine (chia theo book, không phải tables). The man who lives next door is... (chia theo man)
5. There is/are chia theo N sau nó: There is a book, There are two books.
6. The number of + N số nhiều + V số ít (Số lượng...) vs A number of + N số nhiều + V số nhiều (Một số...): The number of students is increasing vs A number of students are waiting.
data.examples:
1. My collection of old stamps is very valuable. I have collected them for 10 years.
   (Bộ sưu tập tem cũ của tôi rất giá trị - chia theo collection, không phải stamps)
2. Everyone in my family is very supportive and kind.
   (Mọi người trong gia đình tôi đều rất ủng hộ và tốt bụng - Everyone + is)
3. There are a lot of interesting books in this library. You should come here.
   (Có rất nhiều sách thú vị trong thư viện này - There are + số nhiều)
4. A number of people are waiting outside. They want to meet the manager.
   (Một số người đang đợi bên ngoài - A number of + are)
5. The number of cars in the city is increasing rapidly. That's why there's so much traffic.
   (Số lượng ô tô trong thành phố đang tăng nhanh - The number of + is)

data.title: Bài 56: The Old Train to Hue
data.transcript: Tuan took the old train from Hanoi to Hue. The train was slow and noisy, but the windows were wide open. He bought a ticket for a hard seat to save money. The train passed through green rice fields, small villages, and tunnels in the mountains. Vendors walked through the carriage selling boiled eggs, sticky rice, and tea. Tuan practiced English with a French tourist sitting next to him. The tourist asked, How long have you been learning English? Tuan answered slowly but clearly. At night, the train lights were dim, and people slept on the floor with blankets. Tuan could not sleep, so he listened to the sound of the wheels. Clack-clack, clack-clack. It sounded like a rhythm. He wrote new words in his notebook: journey, carriage, vendor, tunnel. When the train arrived in Hue at five in the morning, the air was cool and smelled like incense. Tuan realized that fast planes are convenient, but slow trains give you time to see, talk, and think. That slow journey taught him more English than any textbook.

data.title: Bài 57: My First Time in Da Lat
data.transcript: Lisa went to Da Lat for the first time. She had heard it was called the city of eternal spring. The bus arrived early in the morning, and the air was cold. She wore a thick sweater. She rented a small motorbike and drove to a strawberry garden. The owner allowed her to pick strawberries herself. She learned a new word: harvest. She said, I am harvesting strawberries. In the afternoon, she visited a coffee farm where they grow weasel coffee. The farmer explained the process in Vietnamese, and Lisa tried to translate it into English in her head. At night, she went to the night market and ate grilled rice paper, which people call Vietnamese pizza. She sat by Xuan Huong Lake and wrote in her journal. She wrote, Da Lat is quiet, but my mind is loud with new ideas. She decided to create a listening lesson about describing weather and feelings. Cold, foggy, cozy, peaceful. Those words are easy to remember when you feel them. She went back to Hanoi with a bag full of strawberries and a heart full of stories to tell in English.

data.title: Bài 58: A Homestay in Sapa
data.transcript: Tuan stayed in a homestay in Sapa with a Hmong family. The house was made of wood and had no heater. The family spoke very little Vietnamese and almost no English. The mother cooked over a fire, and the children played outside with a dog. Tuan tried to help. He said, Thank you in Hmong language, which he learned from Google: Ua tsaug. The mother smiled brightly. At night, they all sat around the fire. The father played a bamboo flute. The sound was sad and beautiful. Tuan wanted to ask about the song, but he did not have enough words. He used gestures and simple English: Beautiful music. Where learn? The father understood and pointed to his grandfather. Tuan realized that communication is more than words. He spent two days there without internet. He learned to carry water, cook rice, and say good morning in Hmong. When he left, the little girl gave him a handmade bracelet. He still wears it when he codes. He added a lesson in his app called English with Gestures, teaching how to communicate when you do not share a language. Sometimes kindness translates better than any dictionary.

data.title: Bài 59: The Floating Market in Can Tho
data.transcript: Lisa woke up at four in the morning to visit Cai Rang floating market in Can Tho. She took a small boat in the dark. The river was busy even before sunrise. Hundreds of boats sold pineapples, watermelons, and coconuts. Each boat had a long pole with a sample of what they sold hanging on top. Lisa learned this is called a cay beo. She practiced English with a boat vendor who spoke a little English. She asked, How much is a pineapple? The vendor said, Twenty thousand. Very sweet. Lisa bought one and ate it on the boat. The juice dripped down her chin. The boat driver told her that young people now prefer to work in factories, not on the river. The floating market is getting smaller every year. Lisa felt sad. She recorded a video in English about the market to keep its memory. She said, This is not just a market. It is a culture on water. She added this story to the listening section. She wanted students to learn words like floating, bargaining, and sunrise, but also to appreciate traditions that may disappear soon.

data.title: Bài 64: There is/are vs It is
data.theory:
1. There is/are = Có... ở đâu đó (tồn tại): There is a book on the table (Có một cuốn sách trên bàn). There are many people waiting.
2. It is = Nó là... (thời gian, thời tiết, khoảng cách, ý kiến): It is 7 AM, It is raining, It is 5 km from here to school, It is difficult to learn English.
3. Phân biệt: There is a lot of rain (Có nhiều mưa - tồn tại) vs It is raining a lot (Trời đang mưa nhiều - thời tiết)
4. Cấu trúc hay: There seems/appears to be + N (Dường như có...): There seems to be a problem.
data.examples:
1. There is a small cafe near my office. The coffee there is excellent.
   (Có một quán cà phê nhỏ gần văn phòng tôi. Cà phê ở đó rất ngon.)
2. It is very difficult to find a parking space in this area during rush hour.
   (Rất khó tìm chỗ đỗ xe ở khu vực này vào giờ cao điểm - It is + adj + to V)
3. There are too many cars on the road today. That's why we are stuck in traffic.
   (Hôm nay có quá nhiều ô tô trên đường. Đó là lý do kẹt xe.)
4. It is 10 kilometers from my house to the nearest supermarket.
   (Từ nhà tôi đến siêu thị gần nhất là 10km - It is + khoảng cách)
5. Is there anything I can do to help you? - No, thanks. I'm fine.
   (Có gì tôi giúp được không? - Không, cảm ơn. Tôi ổn.)

data.title: Bài 60: Lost in Hoi An Ancient Town
data.transcript: Tuan got lost in Hoi An ancient town at night. All the streets looked the same with yellow walls and red lanterns. His phone battery was dead, so he had no map. He walked around for thirty minutes and could not find his hotel. He decided to ask for help. He saw an old woman selling lanterns. He said in English, Excuse me, I am lost. Can you help me find my hotel? The woman did not understand English, but she called her grandson who spoke a little. The boy asked for the hotel name, and Tuan showed him a paper with the address. The boy pointed and said, Go straight, then left, near the bridge. Tuan thanked them and bought a small lantern as a gift. When he found his hotel, he laughed at himself. He had been building a navigation feature for his app, but he himself got lost. He realized that being lost is a great way to learn English because you must ask for help. He created a lesson called Asking for Directions with useful phrases: I am lost, Could you show me on the map, Is it far from here. Getting lost in Hoi An became one of his favorite memories because it taught him humility and the importance of asking.

data.title: Bài 61: Climbing Fansipan Mountain
data.transcript: Lisa decided to climb Fansipan, the highest mountain in Vietnam. She did not take the cable car. She wanted to climb. The first hour was easy. She sang English songs. The second hour was difficult. Her legs hurt and it rained. She wanted to give up. A porter, a local man who carries bags, walked with her and said, Slowly, slowly. No rush. Lisa repeated in English, Slowly but surely. She learned that proverb that day. After eight hours, she reached the top. The clouds were below her, and the sky was clear. She cried because she was tired and happy. At the top, she met other climbers from different countries. They did not share the same language, but they hugged and took photos together. They all said, We made it. Lisa wrote in her journal, Climbing a mountain is like learning English. At first it is exciting, then it becomes hard and you want to quit. But if you keep going slowly, you will reach the top and the view is worth it. She added a listening lesson about perseverance with words like summit, struggle, and achievement.

data.title: Bài 62: My First Job Interview in English
data.transcript: Tuan still remembers his first job interview in English. He wore a white shirt that was too big and arrived thirty minutes early. His hands were sweaty. The interviewer, a foreign manager, asked, Tell me about yourself. Tuan had memorized a long answer, but he spoke so fast that the manager could not understand. Then the manager asked, What is your biggest weakness? Tuan did not understand the word weakness. He guessed and said, I am very strong. Everyone laughed kindly. He did not get the job. He went home disappointed but not angry. He wrote down every question he did not understand and learned them. He practiced with a mirror for two weeks. In the next interview, he said, My biggest weakness is that I am too detail-oriented, but I am learning to manage my time better. He spoke slowly and clearly. He got the job. Now he teaches his students, An interview is not about perfect English. It is about honest answers and clear communication. Prepare for common questions, but also be ready to say, Could you repeat that please. That sentence can save your interview.

data.title: Bài 63: Working From Home
data.transcript: When the pandemic started, TuanQK Education team had to work from home. At first, Tuan loved it. He could work in pajamas and save time. But after one week, he felt lonely and unproductive. He woke up late and worked from his bed. His back hurt. He decided to create rules for working from home. He woke up at seven, took a shower, and wore a shirt as if going to the office. He created a small workspace with a desk and a plant. He used the Pomodoro technique: twenty-five minutes work, five minutes rest. Every morning, the team had a fifteen-minute video call in English to practice speaking. They said, What did you do yesterday? What will you do today? At first it was awkward, but later it became fun. Tuan learned that working from home needs more discipline than working in an office. He added a listening lesson about remote work vocabulary: deadline, meeting, productivity, distraction. He tells students, Your environment shapes your habits. If you want to be productive, create a space that makes you want to work.

data.title: Bài 64: How TuanQK Team Builds a Feature
data.transcript: Lisa wanted to understand how TuanQK team builds a new feature. Tuan explained it in simple English. First, we listen to users. If many users say, I want to save my favorite words, we write it down. Second, we design. We draw the screen on paper with boxes and arrows. Third, we code. Tuan writes the logic while another developer writes the interface. Fourth, we test. We try to break the app to find bugs. Fifth, we release. We publish the new version and watch if users like it. Lisa asked, What if users don't like it? Tuan said, Then we listen again and improve. It is a circle. He gave an example: The karaoke highlight feature in Music Study. Users said the lyrics were hard to follow. The team added blue highlight that moves with the music. Users loved it. Tuan added a listening lesson about teamwork with words like brainstorm, prototype, feedback, and launch. He said building an app is like building a house. You need a plan, good tools, and a team that communicates clearly in any language.

data.title: Bài 65: The Email That Changed Everything
data.transcript: Tuan received an email in English from a user in Japan. The email said, Your app helped me pass my English exam. I got a job in Vietnam because of it. Thank you. Tuan read it three times. He had never met this user. He was just a small developer in Hanoi, but his app helped someone thousands of kilometers away. He printed the email and put it on the wall. On difficult days when bugs appeared and users complained, he looked at that email. It reminded him why he started. He replied to the user in English and asked for his story. The user said he studied every morning for six months using TuanQK Education. Tuan asked if he could share the story in a listening lesson. The user agreed. That email became lesson 65. Tuan tells his team, One email can change your whole motivation. Always read user feedback carefully. You never know which message will keep you going for the next year. That email is still on the wall today, yellow but inspiring.

data.title: Bài 66: Learning English with AI
data.transcript: Lisa was curious about learning English with AI. She tried talking to an AI chatbot. She said, Hello. The AI replied, Hello, Lisa. How can I help you today? Lisa asked, Can you correct my pronunciation? The AI said, Sure, please speak. Lisa said, I have a cat. The AI said, Good, but your cat sounds like cut. Try to make the a longer. Lisa was amazed. She practiced for one hour every day with AI. She was not afraid of making mistakes because AI never laughed. But after one month, she realized something. AI is good for practice, but it cannot replace human connection. AI does not know how you feel. It does not smile when you make a joke. So she started to use AI for ten minutes to practice grammar, then she talked with real people for twenty minutes. She told her students, Use AI as a mirror to check yourself, but use real people as windows to see the world. She added a listening lesson about AI and language learning with words like artificial, algorithm, and practice partner. AI is a great tool, but human warmth is still the best teacher.

data.title: Bài 67: When the Server Went Down
data.transcript: One Sunday night, the TuanQK Education server went down. Thousands of users could not open the app. Tuan was having dinner with his family. His phone started ringing nonstop. He opened his laptop and saw many error messages. The database was full. He felt panicked. He called his teammate, and they worked together online. They cleaned the old logs and restarted the server. After two hours, the app worked again. Tuan wrote an apology email to users in English. He said, We are sorry for the inconvenience. Our server had a problem, but we fixed it. Thank you for your patience. Many users replied kindly. They said, Thank you for fixing it quickly. We understand. Tuan learned an important lesson. Technology will fail sometimes. What matters is how you communicate when it fails. He added a listening lesson about handling problems with phrases like The system is down, We are working on it, We apologize for the delay. Honest and quick communication builds trust more than perfect technology.

data.title: Bài 68: Mom's Birthday Surprise
data.transcript: Tuan wanted to surprise his mom for her birthday. His mom loves English songs but does not understand the lyrics. Tuan decided to translate her favorite song, You Raise Me Up, into Vietnamese and sing it for her. He practiced for one week. His pronunciation was not perfect, but he sang with love. On her birthday, the family had a small party with noodles and cake. Tuan stood up and said, Mom, this song is for you. He played the guitar and sang in English, then explained each line in Vietnamese. You raise me up means Me nang con len. His mom cried with happiness. She said, This is the best gift I have ever received. Not because of the song, but because you spent time to learn it for me. Tuan recorded the moment and added it as a listening lesson about family love. He teaches students words like surprise, gratitude, and appreciate. He says, The best way to learn English is to use it to make someone you love happy. When you learn with love, you never forget.

data.title: Bài 69: Dad Teaches Me to Ride a Bike
data.transcript: When Tuan was six, his dad taught him to ride a bicycle. His dad held the back of the bike and ran with him. Tuan was scared and shouted, Don't let go. His dad said, I won't. But after a while, his dad secretly let go. Tuan rode alone for ten meters before he realized and fell down. He cried, but his dad hugged him and said, You rode by yourself. You are brave. Now, thirty years later, Tuan teaches his team to ride a bike in English. He says, Learning English is like learning to ride a bike. At first, someone holds you. Your teacher, your app, your dictionary. Then one day, they let go, and you must ride alone. You will fall, but you will also ride. He added a listening lesson about childhood memories with words like balance, fall down, and proud. Every time he rides a bike now, he remembers his dad's hands on the back of his bike. Those hands gave him confidence to ride and to learn.

data.title: Bài 70: Cooking with Grandma
data.transcript: Lisa loves to cook with her grandma. Her grandma is eighty years old and cannot speak English, but she is a great teacher. She teaches by showing, not by telling. One day, they made banh chung for Tet. Her grandma showed her how to wash the leaves, soak the rice, and wrap the cake. Lisa tried to describe each step in English: First, we wash the leaves. Next, we put rice and beans in the middle. Finally, we wrap it tightly. Her grandma nodded even though she did not understand the words. She smiled because Lisa was trying. After eight hours of boiling, they opened the banh chung. It was perfect. Lisa took a photo and wrote a caption in English: Made with grandma, made with love. She added a listening lesson about cooking verbs: wash, soak, wrap, boil. She says, Cooking with grandma taught me that language is not just words. It is patience, observation, and love. When you cook with someone, you learn more than a recipe. You learn their story.

data.title: Bài 71: The Letter I Never Sent
data.transcript: Tuan found an old letter in his drawer. It was a letter he wrote in English to his best friend who moved to America five years ago. The letter said, I miss you. We used to play football every afternoon. Now the field is empty. I am learning English hard so one day I can visit you and we can talk without translation. He never sent the letter because he was shy about his English. Now his English is good, but his friend has a new life and they rarely talk. Tuan felt sad. He decided to send the letter anyway, with a new note: Sorry for being late. My English is better now. Can we talk again? His friend replied the next day, I kept your old football shirt. Let's video call this weekend. They talked for two hours in English and Vietnamese. Tuan learned that it is never too late to send a letter. He added a listening lesson about friendship and time with words like miss, connection, and apologize. He tells students, Don't wait until your English is perfect to contact someone. Perfect English is not required for true friendship.

data.title: Bài 41: Âm /l/ (l)
data.transcript:
1. Hướng dẫn khẩu hình: Đầu lưỡi chạm lợi trên, hơi thoát qua hai bên lưỡi, rung dây thanh. /l/ sáng ở đầu từ, /l/ tối ở cuối từ.
2. Từ vựng ví dụ:
- Love /lʌv/ (yêu)
- Light /laɪt/ (ánh sáng)
- School /skuːl/ (trường)
- Small /smɔːl/ (nhỏ)
- Hello /həˈləʊ/ (xin chào)
3. Câu thực hành: I love the light in the small school, hello!
4. Lưu ý: Phân biệt light /l/ và right /r/.

data.title: Bài 72: My Little Sister's First English Word
data.transcript: Tuan's little sister is four years old. One day, she heard Tuan practicing English. She asked, What does apple mean? Tuan showed her a picture of an apple and said, Apple. She repeated, Apple, apple. She was so happy that she ran to her mom and shouted, Mom, apple. Mom, apple. Her mom laughed and gave her a real apple. From that day, she asked for one new English word every day. Cat, dog, banana, car. She learned very fast because she was not afraid of mistakes. She sang ABC song loudly even though her pronunciation was wrong. Tuan recorded her voice and added it to the app as a listening lesson for beginners. He said, My sister teaches us how to learn. She learns with joy, not fear. She uses words immediately. She is not shy. Adults should learn like children. Don't worry about grammar. Just learn one word and use it today. That little girl's first word, apple, reminded Tuan why he loves teaching. Learning starts with curiosity, not with perfection.

data.title: Bài 73: Sunday Dinner with Family
data.transcript: Every Sunday, Tuan's family has dinner together. No phones are allowed at the table. It is a rule his mom made. They eat fish, vegetables, and rice. They talk about their week. Last Sunday, Tuan's dad asked him in Vietnamese, What did you learn this week? Tuan decided to answer in English to practice. He said, I learned how to fix a bug and how to say sorry professionally. His family did not understand everything, but they listened and clapped. His mom said in Vietnamese, Your English sounds nice. Tuan felt proud. His little sister tried to say, I learned apple. Everyone laughed. After dinner, they washed dishes together and sang a song. Tuan realized Sunday dinner is not just about food. It is about connection. He added a listening lesson about family routines with words like gather, share, and tradition. He tells students, You don't need to go abroad to practice English. You can practice with your family. Teach them one English word during dinner. That small habit makes family time more fun and your English better at the same time.

data.title: Bài 74: Speaking English for 30 Days Straight
data.transcript: Lisa challenged herself to speak English for thirty days straight. No Vietnamese at all when she was alone or with her English club. Day one was very hard. She forgot words and used her hands a lot. Day five was a little better. She started to dream in English. Day ten, she felt more confident. She ordered coffee in English and the barista understood. Day twenty, she had her first phone call in English with a foreign client. She was nervous but she did it. Day thirty, she recorded a video in English about her challenge. She said, I am not fluent yet, but I am not afraid anymore. That is the biggest change. She shared the video online, and many students said they wanted to try the challenge too. Tuan added a 30-day speaking challenge to TuanQK Education. Users who speak every day get a flame badge. Lisa learned that fluency does not come in one day. It comes from thirty days of small courage. You don't need to speak perfectly. You just need to speak every day.

data.title: Bài 75: The Fear of Making Mistakes
data.transcript: Many Vietnamese students are afraid of making mistakes in English. Tuan was too. He remembered one time he said, I am boring instead of I am bored in class. Everyone laughed. He felt embarrassed and did not speak for one week. Later, his teacher told him, Mistakes are proof that you are trying. If you never make mistakes, you never try anything new. Tuan changed his thinking. He started to collect his mistakes in a notebook called My Beautiful Mistakes. He wrote, Today I said she go instead of she goes. I will remember it. After three months, the notebook was full, but his English was much better. He told his students, Your mistakes are your teachers. Don't hide them. Write them down and celebrate them. In TuanQK Education, when AI corrects your pronunciation, it is not to shame you. It is to show you your next step. He added a listening lesson about mindset with words like mistake, embarrassment, and growth. The students who make the most mistakes and learn from them become the most fluent.

data.title: Bài 65: Câu mệnh lệnh & Let's
data.theory:
1. Mệnh lệnh: V0 đầu câu, không chủ ngữ: Open the door, please. Be careful! Don't touch that! Never lie to me again!
2. Let's + V0 = Rủ làm gì cùng nhau: Let's go! Let's have lunch together. Let's not argue (phủ định).
3. Mệnh lệnh lịch sự: Please + V0 / Could you + V0...? / Would you mind + V-ing...?
4. Be + adj: Be quiet! Be patient! Be careful!
5. Dùng trong hướng dẫn, công thức, biển báo: Mix the flour with water. Keep off the grass.
data.examples:
1. Please turn off the lights when you leave the room. Thanks!
   (Làm ơn tắt đèn khi rời phòng nhé. Cảm ơn!)
2. Don't forget to bring your ID card tomorrow. You will need it.
   (Đừng quên mang thẻ căn cước ngày mai. Bạn sẽ cần nó.)
3. Let's meet at 7 PM at the coffee shop near my house, shall we?
   (Mình gặp nhau lúc 7h tối ở quán cà phê gần nhà mình nhé?)
4. Be careful with that hot pan! You might burn yourself.
   (Cẩn thận với cái chảo nóng đó! Bạn có thể bị bỏng.)
5. Take two tablets twice a day after meals. (Hướng dẫn dùng thuốc)
   (Uống 2 viên 2 lần/ngày sau bữa ăn.)

data.title: Bài 76: How I Overcame Shyness
data.transcript: Lisa was very shy when she was young. She never raised her hand in English class even though she knew the answer. She was afraid people would judge her accent. One day, her teacher forced her to present in front of the class. She cried the night before. But she did it. Her voice was small, but she finished. After that, her teacher said, You were shy, but you were brave too. Shy and brave can exist together. Lisa started to practice small brave actions every day. She said hello to one stranger, asked one question in English, and ordered food in English. Slowly, her shyness became smaller and her bravery became bigger. Now she teaches English on camera to thousands of students. She still feels shy sometimes, but she knows how to be brave at the same time. She added a listening lesson about confidence with words like shy, brave, and step out of comfort zone. She tells students, You don't need to stop being shy. You just need to be a little brave every day. Bravery is not the absence of shyness. It is acting despite shyness.

data.title: Bài 77: Running My First 5K
data.transcript: Tuan had never run more than one kilometer. He decided to run a 5K race. He started training. The first day, he could only run for five minutes before he was out of breath. He wanted to quit. But he remembered learning English. At first, you cannot speak much, but you keep going. He ran every morning for one month. He listened to English podcasts while running. He learned words like stamina, pace, and finish line. On race day, it rained. He ran slowly. At kilometer four, his legs hurt badly. He wanted to walk. But people on the street cheered, Co len. He continued. When he crossed the finish line, he cried. He did not win, but he finished. He got a medal. He realized running and learning English are the same. You need training, patience, and cheering from others. He added a listening lesson about health and goals with words like training, perseverance, and achievement. He tells students, Don't compare yourself to fast runners. Just focus on finishing your own race. Every small run makes you stronger.

data.title: Bài 78: The Power of Saying No
data.transcript: Lisa always said yes to everything. Yes to extra work, yes to helping friends, yes to meetings. She was very busy and very tired. Her English study time disappeared because she said yes too much. One day, she said yes to a project she did not like, and she felt angry at herself. She read a book about the power of saying no. The book said, When you say yes to everything, you say no to your own dreams. She started to practice saying no politely in English. She said, Thank you for thinking of me, but I cannot join this time. I need to focus on my studies. At first, people were surprised, but later they respected her time. She had more time to study English and rest. She became happier and more productive. She added a listening lesson about boundaries with phrases like I appreciate the offer, but, I need to prioritize, and Maybe next time. She tells students, Saying no is not rude. It is honest. If you want to learn English well, you must protect your study time. Saying no to distractions is saying yes to your future.

data.title: Bài 79: Saving Money to Study Abroad
data.transcript: Tuan wanted to study abroad, but he had no money. He was a student with a part-time job. He decided to save money. He made a small box and wrote Study Abroad Dream on it. Every day, he put twenty thousand dong into the box. He stopped buying milk tea and new clothes. He cooked at home instead of eating out. His friends laughed and said, Twenty thousand a day will never be enough. But after one year, he saved more than seven million dong. It was not enough for tuition, but it was enough for an English exam and a passport. He passed the exam and got a small scholarship. That scholarship plus his savings allowed him to go to Singapore for a short course. That short course changed his life. He met teachers from different countries and learned new teaching methods. He brought those methods back to TuanQK Education. He tells students, You don't need a lot of money to start. You need a box, a dream, and the discipline to save every day. Small money saved every day becomes a big opportunity one day.

data.title: Bài 80: At the Supermarket
data.transcript: Lisa went to a big supermarket to buy groceries. She decided to practice English by reading all the labels. She learned words like organic, expired, and discount. At the vegetable section, she tried to ask in English, Excuse me, where can I find basil? The staff did not understand, so she showed a picture on her phone. She found the basil. At the checkout, the cashier said, Do you need a bag? Lisa said, Yes, please. She paid and said, Thank you. Have a nice day. It was a small conversation, but she felt proud. She realized a supermarket is a great place to learn English because you see words everywhere. She created a listening lesson called Supermarket English with phrases like How much is this, Is there any discount, and Where is the dairy section. She tells students, You don't need to go to an English speaking country. You can practice in your local supermarket. Read labels, ask questions, and talk to cashiers. Every shopping trip is an English lesson if you want it to be.

data.title: Bài 81: Ordering Coffee in English
data.transcript: Tuan loves coffee, but he was shy to order coffee in English. In a coffee shop with foreign baristas, he always pointed at the menu instead of speaking. One day, he decided to change. He learned a simple script: Hi, I would like a black coffee, please. No sugar. Thank you. He practiced it ten times at home. He went to the coffee shop and said it. The barista smiled and said, Sure. What size? Tuan did not expect that question. He panicked and said, Medium. The barista said, Okay, one medium black coffee. Tuan felt very happy. He realized ordering coffee is a complete conversation with greeting, request, question, and thanks. He added a listening lesson about coffee shop English with phrases like Can I have, To go or to stay, and How much is it. He tells students, Start with coffee. If you can order coffee in English, you can order anything. Coffee is not just a drink. It is a daily chance to practice English with a smile. Now he orders coffee in English every day and his confidence grows like coffee aroma.

data.title: Bài 82: Helping a Tourist in Hanoi
data.transcript: Lisa was walking near Hoan Kiem Lake when a tourist asked her in English, Excuse me, how can I get to the Old Quarter? Lisa was nervous because her English was not perfect, but she wanted to help. She said, Go straight, then turn left. The Old Quarter is near here. The tourist did not understand turn left. Lisa used her hands and said, Left is this way. She pointed. The tourist smiled and said, Thank you. You speak English well. Lisa felt so proud that she walked the tourist to the Old Quarter herself. On the way, they talked. The tourist was from Germany and loved Vietnamese food. Lisa recommended bun cha. After that, Lisa was no longer afraid to speak with foreigners. She realized that tourists do not need perfect grammar. They need direction and kindness. She added a listening lesson about helping tourists with phrases like You are here, It's about ten minutes walk, and Be careful crossing the street. Helping a tourist is a great way to practice English and make a new friend from another country.

data.title: Bài 83: The Rainy Season in Saigon
data.transcript: Tuan moved to Saigon during the rainy season. Every afternoon at three o'clock, it rained heavily for one hour. At first, he was annoyed because his shoes got wet and traffic got stuck. But later, he started to love it. He noticed Saigon people are very good at preparing for rain. They always have a raincoat in their motorbike. When it rains, they stop under a bridge, drink coffee, and wait. They are not angry. They are patient. Tuan learned a new phrase: When it rains, it pours. It means when one bad thing happens, many bad things happen at the same time. But Saigon people laugh and say, Rain is free car wash. He added a listening lesson about weather and attitude with words like drizzle, downpour, and flood. He tells students, You cannot control the rain, but you can control your reaction. If you learn English, there will be rainy days when you feel you make no progress. On those days, just stop, drink coffee, and wait. The rain will stop, and you will continue your journey. Saigon rain taught him patience.

data.title: Bài 84: My Favorite Song in English
data.transcript: Lisa's favorite song in English is Count on Me by Bruno Mars. She first heard it when she was sad and lonely. The lyrics say, You can count on me like one, two, three. I'll be there. She did not understand every word, but she felt the meaning. Friendship. She listened to it every day for one month. She learned the lyrics by heart. She sang it to her best friend on her birthday. Her friend cried. Lisa realized a favorite song is a powerful tool to learn English because you love it, so you repeat it many times without feeling bored. She added a listening series called Learn English with Songs where students learn vocabulary through lyrics. For Count on Me, she teaches count on, lean on, and be there. She tells students, Find a song that touches your heart. Listen, sing, and learn the story behind it. When you learn English with love, you remember forever. Her favorite song is not just music. It is a lesson about friendship that she can now explain in English.

data.title: Bài 85: What Does Happiness Mean?
data.transcript: Tuan asked his students, What does happiness mean in English? One student said, Happiness is a lot of money. Another said, Happiness is traveling. Tuan told them about his grandmother who lives in a small village. She has very little money, no smartphone, and no air conditioner. But she laughs every day. She is happy when her chickens lay eggs, when her flowers bloom, and when her grandchildren visit. She says, Happiness is enough. Tuan realized happiness is not about having more. It is about appreciating what you have. He asked his students to write three things that make them happy in English every day. One student wrote, I am happy because I learned five new words today. Another wrote, I am happy because my mom cooked my favorite soup. Tuan added a listening lesson about gratitude with words like content, appreciate, and enough. He tells students, If you wait to be happy when your English is perfect, you will never be happy. Be happy now because you are learning. Happiness is not the destination. It is the way you walk. That lesson made many students smile and study with more joy.

data.title: Bài 86: My First Computer
data.transcript: Tuan got his first computer when he was twelve. It was an old white desktop with a small screen. The computer had only 256 megabytes of RAM. It was very slow, but Tuan loved it. He turned it on and heard a beep sound. Windows XP started with a green hill picture. He learned how to use a mouse. He clicked, double-clicked, and right-clicked. He opened Notepad and typed his name. He felt like a magician. His father told him, Don't break it. It is expensive. Tuan promised to be careful. Every day after school, he spent one hour learning to type without looking at the keyboard. He learned words like desktop, keyboard, and folder. One day, the computer got a virus and showed a blue screen. He was scared, but he learned how to reinstall Windows from a CD. That old slow computer taught him patience and curiosity. It was the beginning of his journey to become a developer and build TuanQK Education.

data.title: Bài 87: Learning to Design a Logo
data.transcript: Lisa wanted to design a logo for TuanQK Education. She had no experience in design. She opened a free design tool and saw many colors and fonts. She felt confused. Tuan told her, Good design is simple and meaningful. Lisa started with an idea: a book and a graduation cap. She drew many versions on paper. The first logo was too complicated with many colors. The second was too simple and boring. She learned about design principles: balance, contrast, and simplicity. She chose blue because it means trust and learning. She chose a clean font that is easy to read. She showed the logo to students, and they said it looks friendly and educational. She learned a new phrase: Less is more. It means simple is better. Now the TuanQK logo with a book is on every screen of the app. Lisa added a listening lesson about design vocabulary: logo, font, color, and minimal. She tells students, Design is not just about making things beautiful. It is about making things clear and useful for users.

data.title: Bài 88: What is an Operating System
data.transcript: In a listening lesson, Tuan explains what an operating system is in simple English. He says, Imagine your computer is a house. The operating system is the manager of the house. It controls the lights, the doors, and who can enter. Without a manager, the house is messy. Windows, macOS, and Linux are different managers with different styles. Windows is popular and easy to use. macOS is beautiful and expensive. Linux is free and powerful, loved by programmers. The operating system does three important jobs. First, it manages memory. It decides which app can use RAM. Second, it manages files. It keeps your photos and documents organized in folders. Third, it manages hardware. It talks to your keyboard, mouse, and printer. Tuan asks students, What operating system do you use? Many say Windows. Some say Android on their phones, which is also an operating system based on Linux. Understanding operating system helps you understand how your computer thinks.

data.title: Bài 66: Too & Enough - Quá & Đủ
data.theory:
1. Too + adj/adv + to V = quá... đến nỗi KHÔNG thể (tiêu cực): Too expensive to buy (quá đắt nên không thể mua)
2. Adj/Adv + enough + to V = đủ... để có thể (tích cực): Old enough to drive (đủ tuổi để lái xe)
3. Enough + N + to V = đủ N để: I have enough money to buy it.
4. Too many + N đếm được, Too much + N không đếm được (quá nhiều): Too many cars, Too much traffic.
5. Phân biệt: too (quá, tiêu cực) vs very (rất, trung tính): This is too expensive = đắt quá (không mua được) vs This is very expensive = rất đắt (nhưng vẫn có thể mua).
data.examples:
1. This bag is too expensive. I can't afford it.
   (Túi này quá đắt. Tôi không mua nổi - too = không thể)
2. She is old enough to live by herself. She is 20 now.
   (Cô ấy đủ tuổi để sống một mình. Cô ấy 20 tuổi rồi - enough = có thể)
3. Do we have enough chairs for all the guests? Let's count again.
   (Chúng ta có đủ ghế cho tất cả khách không? Đếm lại nhé.)
4. There are too many advertisements on this website. It's annoying.
   (Có quá nhiều quảng cáo trên trang web này. Thật khó chịu.)
5. He speaks too quickly. I can't understand him at all.
   (Anh ấy nói quá nhanh. Tôi không hiểu gì cả.)

data.title: Bài 15: Âm /ɔɪ/ (o-ây)
data.transcript:
Bài 15: Âm /ɔɪ/ (o-ây)

​Hướng dẫn khẩu hình: Bắt đầu phát âm từ âm /ɔ/ với môi tròn, sau đó lướt nhanh sang âm /ɪ/, môi dẹt dần sang hai bên.

​Công thức ghép âm (Tách & Đánh vần):
b /b/ + oy /ɔɪ/ : boy /bɔɪ/
t /t/ + oy /ɔɪ/ : toy /tɔɪ/
v /v/ + oi /ɔɪ/ + ce /s/ : voice /vɔɪs/
p /p/ + oi /ɔɪ/ + nt /nt/ : point /pɔɪnt/
en /ɪn/ + joy /dʒɔɪ/ : enjoy /ɪnˈdʒɔɪ/

​Từ vựng ứng dụng:
Boy /bɔɪ/: con trai
Toy /tɔɪ/: đồ chơi
Voice /vɔɪs/: giọng nói
Point /pɔɪnt/: điểm, chỉ tay
Enjoy /ɪnˈdʒɔɪ/: thưởng thức, yêu thích

​Câu thực hành: The boy enjoys his toy with loud voice and points.
​Lưu ý: Âm /ɔɪ/ là nguyên âm đôi, chuyển khẩu hình mượt mà từ môi tròn (/ɔ/) sang dẹt rộng hai bên (/ɪ/).
Ms. Lisa thanked Tuan Pham for assisting with teaching: Dạ, cô Lisa cám ơn Tuan Phạm đã trợ giảng ạ!

data.title: Bài 89: The First Line of Code
data.transcript: Tuan still remembers his first line of code. He wrote in Pascal: WriteLn('Hello, World'); He pressed Run, and the screen showed Hello, World. He jumped with joy. It was magic. He told his mom, Mom, I talked to the computer and it answered. His mom laughed but was proud. After that, he learned variables. A variable is like a box where you keep something. He wrote, name = Tuan. Age = 15. He learned if statements. If age is more than 18, you can vote. Otherwise, you cannot. He made many mistakes. He forgot semicolons and the program did not run. He learned that computers are very strict. One small mistake and they do not understand. He added a listening lesson about programming basics with words like code, variable, and error. He tells students, Coding is like learning English. You need vocabulary, grammar, and practice. Your first line of code is like your first English word. It opens a new world.

data.title: Bài 90: Understanding UI and UX
data.transcript: Lisa confused UI and UX. Tuan explained with a coffee shop example. UI is User Interface. It is what you see: the color of the walls, the shape of the cups, the menu design. UX is User Experience. It is how you feel: Is it easy to order? Is the chair comfortable? Is the service fast? A beautiful UI with bad UX is like a beautiful cup with bad coffee. People will not come back. In TuanQK Education app, the UI is the blue buttons, the icons, and the fonts. The UX is how easy it is to find a lesson, how fast the audio loads, and how clear the feedback is. Tuan says, We design UI with our eyes, but we design UX with our hearts. We must think like a student who is tired after work and wants to learn quickly. Lisa learned to test UX by watching real users use the app. She saw where they got confused and fixed it. She added a listening lesson with words like interface, experience, and user-friendly. Good UI makes you smile. Good UX makes you stay.

data.title: Bài 91: The E-commerce Dream
data.transcript: TuanQK Education started as a free app, but Tuan dreamed of e-commerce. He wanted to sell courses, books, and T-shirts with English slogans. He learned what e-commerce means: buying and selling on the internet. He studied Amazon and Shopee. He learned words like cart, checkout, payment, and shipping. He built a small shop inside the app. Users could add a course to their cart and pay with a bank card. The first sale was a course called 100 Common English Phrases. A student from Da Nang bought it for 99,000 dong. Tuan was so happy that he printed the order and put it on the wall. He realized e-commerce is not just technology. It is trust. People only pay if they trust your product. He added secure payment, clear return policy, and customer reviews. He added a listening lesson about online shopping with phrases like Add to cart, Proceed to checkout, and Your order has been shipped. E-commerce taught him that good education can also be a sustainable business.

data.title: Bài 92: How a Website Works
data.transcript: Many students use websites but do not know how they work. Tuan explains in simple English. When you type www.tuanqk.education and press enter, your computer asks a DNS server, Where is this website? DNS is like a phone book. It translates the name to an IP address, like 192.168.1.1. Then your browser sends a request to that server. The server is a powerful computer far away that stores the website files. It sends back HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML is the structure, like bones. CSS is the style, like clothes. JavaScript is the action, like muscles. Your browser combines them and shows you a beautiful page. If the server is slow, the page loads slowly. If the internet is weak, you see a loading icon. Tuan asks students to open the browser inspector and see the code. He says, Every website you love is just text files. If you learn HTML, you can build your own. Understanding how a website works makes you less scared of technology.

data.title: Bài 93: The Power of a Database
data.transcript: TuanQK Education has 705 lessons. How does the app remember your progress? Tuan explains databases. A database is like a giant Excel sheet. It has tables, rows, and columns. One table is called users. It has columns like id, name, and email. Another table is called lessons. It has id, title, and transcript. Another table is called progress. It connects users and lessons and says which lesson is completed. When you finish Lesson 5, the app writes in the database: user 101 completed lesson 5. He uses Supabase, which is a modern database that works like magic. You can add a lesson from your laptop and it appears in the app immediately. He learned SQL, a language to talk to databases. SELECT means show me. INSERT means add. UPDATE means change. DELETE means remove. He tells students, Data is the memory of an app. Without a database, an app forgets everything when you close it. With a database, it remembers and helps you continue learning. That is why your 500/705 progress never disappears.

data.title: Bài 94: Designing for Mobile First
data.transcript: At first, TuanQK Education was designed for computers. The buttons were small and text was tiny on phones. Users complained, I cannot tap the button. My fingers are too big. Tuan learned about mobile-first design. It means design for the small phone screen first, then for the big computer screen. On mobile, fingers are the mouse. Buttons must be big, at least 48 pixels. Text must be large enough to read without zooming. Important actions should be at the bottom where thumbs can reach. Tuan redesigned the whole app. He put the navigation bar at the bottom with four icons: Trang Chinh, Ngu phap, Tu vung, Ho So. He made the GHI AM button red and big so users can tap easily. After the redesign, users said the app feels much easier. He added a listening lesson about mobile design with words like responsive, thumb-friendly, and portrait. He tells his team, Most of our users learn on the bus or in bed with one hand. If we design for mobile first, we respect their real life.

data.title: Bài 95: What is Cloud Storage
data.transcript: Lisa's phone storage was full. She could not take photos. Tuan told her about cloud storage. He said, Cloud is not a real cloud in the sky. It is many powerful computers in data centers. When you upload to Google Drive or Cloudinary, your files go to those computers. Your phone only keeps a small link. That is why you can see your photos even when your phone is broken. TuanQK Education uses Cloudinary to store videos like YouCut_20260827_214341336.mp4. When a student clicks Lesson 1, the app does not download the whole video. It streams from the cloud. This saves phone storage. He explains benefits: First, you can access files from any device. Second, files are safe even if you lose your phone. Third, you can share a link easily. He also warns about internet. Cloud needs internet. No internet, no cloud. He added a listening lesson with words like upload, download, and backup. He tells students, Don't keep important files only on one device. Put them in the cloud. It is like keeping your money in a bank, not under your pillow.

data.title: Bài 96: The Art of Debugging
data.transcript: Debugging is finding and fixing errors in code. Tuan says it is like being a detective. One day, the listening feature did not play audio. Users pressed the speaker icon and nothing happened. Tuan checked the code. He added logs, which are messages that show what the app is doing. He saw, File not found. He realized the transcript was empty for some lessons. He fixed it by adding a check: If transcript is empty, show No audio available. The bug was fixed. He learned debugging steps: First, reproduce the bug. Can you make it happen again? Second, read the error log. What does it say? Third, guess and test. Try a small fix. Fourth, test again. He tells his team, Don't be afraid of bugs. Every programmer has bugs. Good programmers are good debuggers. He added a listening lesson with words like bug, log, and fix. Debugging teaches patience. Sometimes you search for hours for a missing comma. When you find it, you feel like you found gold.
